written: 2026-11-20, after SeedLM-19, before any SeedLM-20 coder was trained
motivation: Prefix coders lifted the coder-only vote on the development fifth from 61.4 to 64.6 (SeedLM-17, 18), within half a task of the engine (65). The five prefix coders so far were trained on SeedLM-3's data only; the post-coders gained most on held-out teacher tasks from the later data (variants, composed tasks) and from short training
hypothesis: Prefix coders trained on the later data add more to the coder-only vote on real tasks, enough to pass the engine
coders: three prefix coders, s3b-pyx's architecture, 40 minutes, seeds 4, 5 and 6, with the seeded variants and the composed tasks at a tenth of the rows each: scripts/seedlm3_train.py --name s20-p<seed> --minutes 40 --d-model 320 --layers 8 --heads 10 --views 3 --seed <seed> --variant-share 0.1 --compose-share 0.1; nothing else runs while they train
primary_measure: development fifth, coders alone: the vote of all twenty-one cached coders (ties to the shortest program, mean over 200 orders; scripts/seedlm16_occam.py). Supported if above 65.5 (more than the engine's 65); not supported if below 64.6 (eighteen coders); inconclusive otherwise
secondary_measures: held-out teacher tasks, the same vote (eighteen coders: 72.25)
each new prefix coder alone, against s18-p1..p3 (development 55, 60, 56; teacher 45, 42, 45)
choice: diagnostic; the system's adoption rule is unchanged
note_1: s20-p5's first run was stopped by a container restart at about 30 of its 40 minutes, before any measurement of it; it was rerun from the start with the same arguments. s20-p4 had finished and been cached before the restart (alone: teacher 49, development 54)
note_2: The rerun of s20-p5 went slower than s20-p4 in the fresh container (1,713 steps in 40 minutes against 1,808; s20-p6 1,749); nothing else ran during training apart from a few seconds of light scripts

outcome.primary: development fifth, the vote of all twenty-one coders: 64.63 (sd 0.51 over 200 orders, 63 to 65; eighteen coders 64.57). Between 64.6 and 65.5: inconclusive, in effect unchanged (reports/seedlm/ensemble_occam_21.json)
secondary: held-out teacher tasks, the same vote: 71.23 (eighteen coders 72.25)
outcome.reported: tasks some coder solves (counts only): development 71 with or without the three new coders, which solve no development task no other coder solves (the three alone reach 61, s18-p1..p3 64); teacher 97 -> 100
outcome.reading: The later data made the prefix coders better on generated tasks and no better on real ones: alone they lost about 4 development tasks against the SeedLM-3-data prefix coders, and in the vote they added nothing on the development fifth and cost one task on the teacher tasks. What the first five prefix coders added on real tasks did not come from their architecture alone; with three seeds a side the data and seed effects are not separated
